chapter_sections.label: Definition:
chapter_sections.text: - AREAS RELATED TO CIRCLES is the study of calculating the areas and arc lengths of parts of a circle, namely the SECTOR and the SEGMENT, using the known formula for the area of a full circle.

chapter_sections.label: Key Points:
points: A CIRCLE is a closed curve where all points are at equal distance (radius) from the centre.
Parts of a circle studied in this chapter: SECTOR and SEGMENT.
All formulae in this chapter are derived using the UNITARY METHOD.
Unless stated otherwise, "sector" means MINOR SECTOR and "segment" means MINOR SEGMENT.
Value of pi (π) used: 22/7 (unless stated otherwise in the problem).

chapter_sections.label: LIST OF TOPICS IN THIS CHAPTER:
items: - Topic 11.1: Areas of Sector and Segment of a Circle
(Note: This chapter has only ONE topic as per textbook. Mode B — no sub-topics invented.)

items.question: What is a sector of a circle? Name its two types.
items.answer:
A SECTOR of a circle is the portion of the circular region enclosed by two radii and the corresponding arc.
Types:
- MINOR SECTOR: The smaller sector (region OAPB).
- MAJOR SECTOR: The larger sector (region OAQB).
Angle of major sector = 360° − angle of minor sector.

items.question: What is a segment of a circle? Name its two types.
items.answer:
A SEGMENT of a circle is the portion of the circular region enclosed between a chord and the corresponding arc.
Types:
- MINOR SEGMENT: The smaller segment (region APB).
- MAJOR SEGMENT: The larger segment (region AQB).
Note: Unless stated otherwise, "segment" means MINOR SEGMENT.

items.question: State the formula for the area of a sector of a circle with radius r and angle θ (in degrees). Also state the formula for the length of its arc.
items.answer:
Area of sector = (θ / 360) × π × r²

Length of arc = (θ / 360) × 2 × π × r

where r = radius of the circle and θ = angle of the sector in degrees.

items.question: State the formula for the area of a segment of a circle. How is it related to the sector?
items.answer:
Area of segment APB = Area of sector OAPB − Area of triangle OAB
= (θ / 360) × π × r² − Area of triangle OAB

The segment is part of the sector; the triangular region OAB must be subtracted from the sector to get the segment area.

---

items.question: Find the area of a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm if the angle of the sector is 60°. (Use π = 22/7)
items.answer:
Given: r = 6 cm, θ = 60°, π = 22/7

Step 1: Write the formula.
Area of sector = (θ / 360) × π × r²

Step 2: Substitute values.
= (60 / 360) × (22/7) × 6 × 6
= (1/6) × (22/7) × 36

Step 3: Simplify.
= (1/6) × (792/7)
= 792 / 42
= 132 / 7
= 18.86 cm² (approx.)

Answer: Area of sector = 132/7 cm² ≈ 18.86 cm²

items.question: The length of the minute hand of a clock is 14 cm. Find the area swept by the minute hand in 5 minutes. (Use π = 22/7)
items.answer:
Given: r = 14 cm, π = 22/7

Step 1: Find the angle swept in 5 minutes.
In 60 minutes, minute hand completes 360°.
In 5 minutes, angle swept = (5/60) × 360° = 30°.

Step 2: Write the formula.
Area swept = (θ / 360) × π × r²

Step 3: Substitute and calculate.
= (30 / 360) × (22/7) × 14 × 14
= (1/12) × (22/7) × 196
= (1/12) × (22 × 28)
= (1/12) × 616
= 51.33 cm² (approx.)

Answer: Area swept = 616/12 cm² ≈ 51.33 cm²

items.question: Derive the formula for the area of a sector using the Unitary Method. (r = radius, θ = angle in degrees)
items.answer:
Given: A circle of radius r with a sector of angle θ.

Step 1: Area of the full circle (angle 360°) = π × r²

Step 2: By Unitary Method:
When angle = 360°, area = π × r²
When angle = 1°,   area = π × r² / 360

Step 3: When angle = θ°:
Area of sector = (θ / 360) × π × r²

This formula gives the area of a sector with any angle θ in a circle of radius r.

---

items.question: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends a right angle at the centre. Find the area of the corresponding: (i) minor segment (ii) major sector. (Use π = 3.14)
items.answer:
Given: r = 10 cm, θ = 90°, π = 3.14

Step 1: Find the area of the minor sector (θ = 90°).
Area of minor sector = (90/360) × 3.14 × 10 × 10
= (1/4) × 314
= 78.5 cm²

Step 2: Find the area of triangle OAB.
Since θ = 90°, the triangle OAB is a right-angled triangle.
OA = OB = r = 10 cm (both are radii).
Area of triangle OAB = (1/2) × OA × OB
= (1/2) × 10 × 10
= 50 cm²

Step 3: Find the area of minor segment.
Area of minor segment = Area of minor sector − Area of triangle OAB
= 78.5 − 50
= 28.5 cm²

Step 4: Find the area of major sector.
Area of major sector = π × r² − Area of minor sector
= 3.14 × 100 − 78.5
= 314 − 78.5
= 235.5 cm²

Answer: (i) Area of minor segment = 28.5 cm²
(ii) Area of major sector = 235.5 cm²

items.question: In a circle of radius 21 cm, an arc subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find: (i) the length of the arc (ii) area of the sector formed by the arc (iii) area of the segment formed by the corresponding chord. (Use π = 22/7)
items.answer:
Given: r = 21 cm, θ = 60°, π = 22/7

Step 1: Length of the arc.
Length = (θ / 360) × 2 × π × r
= (60/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 21
= (1/6) × 2 × (22/7) × 21
= (1/6) × 2 × 66
= (1/6) × 132
= 22 cm

Step 2: Area of the sector.
Area = (θ / 360) × π × r²
= (60/360) × (22/7) × 21 × 21
= (1/6) × (22/7) × 441
= (1/6) × 1386
= 231 cm²

Step 3: Area of triangle OAB.
For θ = 60° and OA = OB = 21 cm, triangle OAB is equilateral.
Side = r = 21 cm.
Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) × 21²
= (√3 / 4) × 441
= 441√3 / 4
≈ (441 × 1.732) / 4
≈ 763.812 / 4
≈ 190.95 cm²

Step 4: Area of segment.
Area = Area of sector − Area of triangle OAB
= 231 − 190.95
= 40.05 cm² (approx.)

Answer: (i) Length of arc = 22 cm
(ii) Area of sector = 231 cm²
(iii) Area of segment ≈ 40.05 cm²

items.question: An umbrella has 8 ribs which are equally spaced. Assuming the umbrella to be a flat circle of radius 45 cm, find the area between two consecutive ribs of the umbrella. (Use π = 22/7)
items.answer:
Given: Number of ribs = 8, r = 45 cm, π = 22/7

Step 1: Find the angle between two consecutive ribs.
Total angle = 360°
Angle between 2 consecutive ribs = 360° / 8 = 45°

Step 2: Area between two consecutive ribs = Area of sector with angle 45°.
Area = (θ / 360) × π × r²

Step 3: Substitute values.
= (45 / 360) × (22/7) × 45 × 45
= (1/8) × (22/7) × 2025

Step 4: Simplify.
= (22 × 2025) / (8 × 7)
= 44550 / 56
= 795.54 cm² (approx.)

Answer: Area between two consecutive ribs = 44550/56 cm² ≈ 795.54 cm²

items.question: A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a square shaped grass field of side 15 m by means of a 5 m long rope. Find: (i) the area of the field in which the horse can graze. (ii) the increase in the grazing area if the rope were 10 m long instead of 5 m. (Use π = 3.14)
items.answer:
Given: Side of square field = 15 m, rope length (radius) = 5 m initially, then 10 m.

Step 1: Find the angle available at the corner of a square.
Interior angle of square = 90°.
So the horse can graze in a sector of angle 90°.

Step 2: (i) Grazing area with rope = 5 m.
Area = (90/360) × π × r²
= (1/4) × 3.14 × 5 × 5
= (1/4) × 78.5
= 19.625 m²

Step 3: (ii) Grazing area with rope = 10 m.
Note: Side of square = 15 m > 10 m, so the full sector fits in the field.
Area = (90/360) × π × r²
= (1/4) × 3.14 × 10 × 10
= (1/4) × 314
= 78.5 m²

Step 4: Increase in grazing area.
Increase = 78.5 − 19.625 = 58.875 m²

Answer: (i) Grazing area with 5 m rope = 19.625 m²
(ii) Increase in grazing area = 58.875 m²

---

items.question: Find the area of the segment AYB shown in the figure, if the radius of the circle is 21 cm and ∠AOB = 120°. (Use π = 22/7)
items.answer:
Given: r = 21 cm, θ = 120°, π = 22/7

PART A — Area of Minor Segment AYB:

Step 1: Write the relation.
Area of segment AYB = Area of sector OAYB − Area of triangle OAB  ...(1)

Step 2: Find area of sector OAYB.
Area of sector = (θ / 360) × π × r²
= (120/360) × (22/7) × 21 × 21
= (1/3) × (22/7) × 441
= (1/3) × 1386
= 462 cm²  ...(2)

Step 3: Find area of triangle OAB.
Draw OM perpendicular to AB.
Since OA = OB (radii), by RHS congruence:
Triangle AMO ≅ Triangle BMO.
So M is the mid-point of AB.
Angle AOM = Angle BOM = (1/2) × 120° = 60°.

From triangle OMA:
cos 60° = OM/OA → OM/21 = 1/2 → OM = 21/2 cm
sin 60° = AM/OA → AM/21 = √3/2 → AM = 21√3/2 cm

AB = 2 × AM = 21√3 cm

Area of triangle OAB = (1/2) × AB × OM
= (1/2) × 21√3 × (21/2)
= 441√3/4 cm²  ...(3)

Step 4: Find area of minor segment AYB.
= 462 − 441√3/4   [From (1), (2), (3)]
= (1848 − 441√3) / 4
= (21/4)(88 − 21√3) cm²
≈ (21/4)(88 − 21 × 1.732)
≈ (21/4)(88 − 36.372)
≈ (21/4)(51.628)
≈ (21 × 51.628) / 4
≈ 1084.188 / 4
≈ 271.05 cm²

PART B — Area of Major Segment:

Step 5: Find area of major segment.
Area of major segment = π × r² − Area of minor segment
= (22/7) × 21 × 21 − 271.05
= (22/7) × 441 − 271.05
= 1386 − 271.05
= 1114.95 cm² (approx.)

Answer:
Area of minor segment AYB = (21/4)(88 − 21√3) cm² ≈ 271.05 cm²
Area of major segment     ≈ 1114.95 cm²

topics.topic_name: AREAS OF SECTOR AND SEGMENT OF A CIRCLE

sections.label: Definition:
sections.text:
- SECTOR: The portion (or part) of the circular region enclosed by two radii and the corresponding arc is called a SECTOR of the circle.
- SEGMENT: The portion (or part) of the circular region enclosed between a chord and the corresponding arc is called a SEGMENT of the circle.

sections.label: Key Points:
points: OAPB is the MINOR SECTOR (smaller region between two radii and arc APB).
OAQB is the MAJOR SECTOR (larger region between two radii and arc AQB).
The angle AOB is called the ANGLE OF THE SECTOR.
Angle of the major sector = 360° − angle of the minor sector (angle AOB).
APB is the MINOR SEGMENT (smaller region between chord AB and arc APB).
AQB is the MAJOR SEGMENT (larger region between chord AB and arc AQB).
REMARK: When we write "segment" and "sector" we will mean the "minor segment" and the "minor sector" respectively, unless stated otherwise.
All formulae are derived using the UNITARY METHOD.
(Note: Textbook has no sub-topics under Topic 11.1. Mode B — no sub-topics invented.)
theta = angle of the sector at the centre (in degrees)
When angle = 360°, area of sector = πr² (full circle)
When angle = 1°,   area of sector = πr² / 360
When angle = theta°, area of sector = (theta/360) × πr²
FORMULA 2: Length of Arc of Sector
theta = angle of the sector at the centre (in degrees)
Area of segment APB = Area of sector OAPB − Area of triangle OAB
Area of major sector OAQB = πr² − Area of minor sector OAPB
Area of major segment AQB = πr² − Area of minor segment APB
EXAMPLE 11.1.1: Area of Sector and Corresponding Major Sector
PROBLEM: Find the area of the sector of a circle with radius 4 cm and of angle 30°. Also find the area of the corresponding major sector. (Use π = 3.14)
Step 1: Find area of minor sector OAPB.
Step 2: Find area of major sector.
Method 1: Area of major sector = πr² − area of minor sector
Method 2 (Alternative): Area of major sector = ((360 − theta)/360) × πr²
ANSWER: Area of minor sector = 4.19 cm² (approx.), Area of major sector = 46.1 cm² (approx.)
PROBLEM: Find the area of the segment AYB shown in the figure, if radius of the circle is 21 cm and angle AOB = 120°. (Use π = 22/7)
Area of segment AYB = Area of sector OAYB − Area of triangle OAB  ...(1)
Step 2: Find Area of sector OAYB.
Step 3: Find Area of triangle OAB.
Since OA = OB, by RHS congruence, triangle AMO ≅ triangle BMO.
So M is mid-point of AB and angle AOM = angle BOM = (1/2) × 120° = 60°.
Area of triangle OAB = (1/2) × AB × OM
Step 4: Find Area of segment AYB.
ANSWER: Area of segment AYB = (21/4)(88 − 21√3) cm²

11. A car has two wipers which do not overlap. Each wiper has a blade of length 25 cm sweeping through an angle of 115°. Find the total area cleaned at each sweep of the blades.

(Use sqrt(3) = 1.7)

(B) (p/180) × πR²
(C) (p/360) × 2R

OM = 21 cos 60° = 21/2 cm
AM = 21 sin 60° = 21√3/2 cm
AB = 21√3 cm

Area of △OAB = (1/2) × 21√3 × (21/2)
= 441√3/4 cm²  ...(3)

Step 4: Area of minor segment.
= 462 − 441√3/4
= (21/4)(88 − 21√3) cm²
≈ (21/4)(88 − 36.37)
≈ (21 × 51.63)/4
≈ 271.05 cm²

PART B — Area of Major Segment:

Step 5: Area of major segment = πr² − Area of minor segment
= (22/7) × 441 − 271.05
= 1386 − 271.05
= 1114.95 cm² (approx.)

Answer:
Area of minor segment AYB = (21/4)(88 − 21√3) cm² ≈ 271.05 cm²
Area of major segment     ≈ 1114.95 cm²

items.question: The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and angle theta (in degrees) is:
items.explanation: Area of sector = (theta/360) × πr². Derived by Unitary Method on full circle area πr².

The length of the arc of a sector with radius r and angle theta (in degrees) is:
items.explanation: Length of arc = (theta/360) × 2πr, derived by Unitary Method on circumference 2πr.

items.question: A quadrant of a circle has an angle of:
items.explanation: A quadrant is 1/4 of a circle. 360° / 4 = 90°.

items.question: Which of the following is the region enclosed between a chord and the corresponding arc?
items.explanation: A SEGMENT is the portion of the circular region enclosed between a chord and the corresponding arc.
